rounds.text: Permanent Magnets Ltd is demonstrating an explosive acceleration in profitability, underscored by a massive 42% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a 96% year-on-year net profit surge [E63]. This earnings momentum translates directly into elite cash generation, highlighted by an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 1.55x alongside ₹31 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026, meaning reported profits are fully and robustly backed by actual cash [E34, E35]. Furthermore, the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22x as of March 2026 [E38], while delivering a healthy 17.8% ROCE [E12] and a phenomenal 22% median return on equity over a 10-year horizon [E26]. When evaluated against sector benchmarks, the business trades at a remarkably modest EV/EBITDA of 14.1x compared to the towering sector median of 329.57x [E11], and offers a very attractive price-to-book ratio of 3.47x against a sector benchmark of 5.75x [E7]. Conceded: the stock carries a rich headline P/E of 34x alongside a DCF model pointing to overvaluation [E1, E65], yet this overlooks a live fundamental turnaround where recent results score 100/100 and profit growth outpaces stale market sentiment [E67].

Permanent Magnets Ltd carries an extreme valuation disconnect supported by adverse fundamental trends in profitability and price performance. A discounted cash flow analysis values the intrinsic worth at Rs 396 per share compared to the current market price of Rs 855, resulting in a severe margin of safety deficit of -116.2% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the market price already prices in an aggressive 16.6% earnings growth rate, which significantly outpaces the 6.0% assumed in the base case [E47]. This rich pricing at a P/E of 34 and a price-to-book of 4.45x leaves no room for error, especially as operating margins have compressed by 6 percentage points from 23% three years ago to 17% in March 2026 [E1, E2, E30, E66]. Compounded profit growth and share price growth over a three-year horizon have both turned negative at -10% and -18% respectively, alongside a high annualised volatility of 82.4% and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -87.4% [E20, E24, E53, E54]. Institutional confidence is practically nonexistent, with foreign institutions holding 0.00% and domestic institutions holding a negligible 0.01% as of June 2026 [E42, E43]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent numbers including a net profit increase of 96% YoY, an operating cash flow of Rs 31 Cr in March 2026, and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22x [E35, E38, E63, E67].

The bear relies heavily on the standard DCF output of Rs 396 [E45], but ignores the fundamental reality that results are currently accelerating with net profit up 96% year-over-year and recent profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 49%, indicating that stale sentiment is missing an active turnaround [E57, E63, E67]. Conceded: the DCF overvalued flag and reverse DCF expectations are as stated [E45, E47, E65], yet these static models miss the company's strong recent operational execution, including an operating cash flow of Rs 31 Cr and robust cash conversion of 1.55x where profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Conceded: three-year profit and share price growth are negative [E20, E24], but the trailing twelve months tell a vastly different and superior story with profit growth surging by 42% [E21] alongside a 3 percentage point quarterly operating margin expansion to 15% in March 2026 [E31]. Conceded: operating margins dropped over a three-year window [E30], but the business remains conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22x [E38] and an EV/EBITDA of 14.1x that trades at a massive discount to the sector benchmark of 329.57x [E11].

The bull flags a 96% year-over-year net profit surge and outperformance [E57, E63, E67], but ignores that the same dataset shows three-year profit and share price growth at -10% and -18% [E20, E24], proving that a single trailing period is masking a longer structural stagnation. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 31 Cr with a 1.55x cash conversion [E34, E35], yet borrowings jumped simultaneously from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 37 Cr [E39], meaning cash generation has not prevented a substantial build-up in debt. Conceded: the TTM profit growth hit 42% and quarterly margins expanded by 3 percentage points [E21, E31], but the broader multi-year trend reveals an operating margin compression of 6 percentage points down to 17% alongside an "Inconsistent" yearly stability reading [E30, E32]. Conceded: the EV/EBITDA is 14.1x versus a lofty sector benchmark [E11], but the absolute valuation still demands a steep 16.6% earnings growth rate just to justify the current ₹ 855 price [E47], far outpacing the base-case assumption of 6.0% [E47]. Finally, citing these green shoots ignores the glaring -116.2% margin of safety and a rich price-to-book of 4.45x [E2, E46], leaving the stock dangerously exposed to any reversion in its highly volatile 82.4% annualized return profile [E54].
